asymmetrical.def: An organizational imbalance where unequal distribution of information between superiors and subordinates causes friction, mismatched expectations, and strategic failure.
asymmetrical.l1: 非対称なコミュニケーション / 情報の非対称性 (情報格差による認識のズレ)

spearheaded.def: To act as the decisive vanguard or primary driving force of an executive project, turnaround, or commercial initiative.
spearheaded.quote: Louie (26:36): "And another nice word to be like, to take in charge is spearheaded. 'I spearheaded the project, I spearheaded the initiative.'"
spearheaded.l1: 陣頭指揮を執った / 主導した / 先頭に立って推進した

mandate.def: An authoritative executive directive, formal scope of authority, or explicit strategic objective commissioned by an organization.
mandate.quote: Louie (26:36): "Now, for the task... we can say my mandate. My main mandate... my primary mandate was to deliver the project on time and under budget."
mandate.l1: 所命 / 委任事項 / 組織から託された最重要ミッション

autonomy.def: The condition of having operational freedom, independence, and full discretionary authority to make decisions without micromanagement.
autonomy.quote: Louie (42:09): "So you like them to have their own autonomy, self-autonomy. Yeah, they have their own self-autonomy."
autonomy.l1: 自律性 / 裁量権 (上司の過度な介入を受けず自走する自由)

anticipate.def: To proactively foresee, calculate, and address a stakeholder's latent priorities, concerns, or requirements before they are voiced.
anticipate.quote: Louie (38:20): "Anticipate his needs... Yes, so you would think, what would he need? I've seen this situation, and I know him. So now I have to anticipate what he would need from me."
anticipate.l1: 相手のニーズを先回りして察知する / 先手を打って対応する

qualitative.def: Pertaining to narrative descriptions, subjective experiences, contextual customer behavior, and quality rather than numerical measurements.
qualitative.quote: YH (12:37): "...and get the hypothesis from here and combine qualitative information and quantitative information to deliver some results."
qualitative.l1: 定性的な / 質的な (数値化できない背景や顧客心理)

quantitative.def: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quantity, volume, or numerical data of something.
quantitative.quote: YH (12:37): "...combine qualitative information and quantitative information to deliver some results."
quantitative.l1: 定量的な / 数値的な (データや指標に基づく)

hypothesis.def: A proposed explanation or commercial assumption formulated as a starting point for further data analysis and strategic testing.
hypothesis.quote: YH (12:37): "I always do the data analysis and get the hypothesis from here..."
hypothesis.l1: 仮説 (データ分析や施策の前提となる仮の結論)

micromanagement.def: A suffocating management style characterized by excessive control, close observation of trivial details, and refusal to grant autonomy.
micromanagement.quote: YH (41:29): "So I don't like to do micro-management, so I trust my subordinates and delegate all the tasks."
micromanagement.l1: マイクロマネジメント / 細部に至る過度な干渉・管理

delegate.def: To entrust operational authority, responsibility, and decision-making to team members and direct reports.
delegate.quote: YH (41:29): "...I give clear direction, but only the big picture and delegate all the tasks to them..."
delegate.l1: 権限委譲する / 業務を任せる

subordinates.def: Persons under the authority, supervision, or operational guidance of an executive or department lead.
subordinates.quote: YH (41:29): "...so I trust my subordinates and delegate all the tasks."
subordinates.l1: 部下 / 統括下の人員

hierarchy.def: A structured system of tiered authority where organizational layers govern reporting relationships and strategic delegation.
hierarchy.quote: YH (42:47): "Well, we have a few layers of that hierarchy. The management layer."
hierarchy.l1: 組織階層 / 階層構造

span-of-control.def: The optimal number of subordinates or regional leads directly managed by an executive to maintain focus and efficiency.
span-of-control.quote: YH (42:47): "So technically I only need to handle these four or five people. Then they will manage their own team. So yeah, this is how I managed over a hundred people."
span-of-control.l1: 統率スパン / 直接管理可能人数

circuit-breaker.def: A pre-engineered checkpoint or milestone audit installed halfway through an initiative to evaluate quality and arrest failure before delivery.
circuit-breaker.quote: Louie (24:48): "And I now implement half, because of that, half-goal circuit breakers... So when there's a test, I test halfway between that just to make sure there's not a problem."
circuit-breaker.l1: 中間安全遮断器 / チェックポイント (重大事故を防ぐ中間監査)

chewed-out.def: To be harshly and loudly scolded or formally reprimanded by a superior for failing to uphold executive standards.
chewed-out.quote: Louie (26:36): "So it was a huge lesson. I got chewed out. I thought I was going to be fired. My boss was super unhappy..."
chewed-out.l1: 大目玉を食らった / 上司から激しく叱責された

inadequate.def: Lacking the required depth, standard, or competence to fulfill an operational requirement or business role.
inadequate.quote: Louie (24:48): "What would happen is the training was inadequate, and then I was inadequate. Then my boss would say to me, 'Why did you not notice that the training was inadequate?'"
inadequate.l1: 不十分な / 力不足の / 基準に満たない

inferior.def: Noticeably lower in operational quality, value, or professional rigor compared with accepted standards.
inferior.quote: Louie (26:36): "The in-house training we got from that company was inferior, but not inferior from that individual, from the trainer..."
inferior.l1: 劣った / 粗悪な / 質の低い

leave-money-on-the-table.def: To surrender, forfeit, or fail to collect additional commercial margin and revenue that a buyer was fully prepared to pay.
leave-money-on-the-table.quote: Louie (26:36): "If I go to a cocktail bar in Japan, they will ask, 'What kind of whiskey do you like?' you know, because they don't want to leave money on the table."
leave-money-on-the-table.l1: 取れるはずの利益を取りこぼす / 付加価値を換金し損ねる

bad-salesmanship.def: Rigid, unimaginative, or defensive selling practices that alienate willing customers and reject revenue opportunities.
bad-salesmanship.quote: Louie (26:36): "I hate having owned a bar because I know how horrible this is. This is very bad salesmanship. Very bad."
bad-salesmanship.l1: 稚拙なセールス対応 / 顧客心理を無視した無策な商売

sing-your-praises.def: To confidently speak of one's own capabilities, direct leadership impact, and professional triumphs without false modesty.
sing-your-praises.quote: Louie (14:02): "Because it's okay to sing your praises, okay? Because that's why you're there to show what you did."
sing-your-praises.l1: 自分の功績や強みを堂々とアピールする / 自賛する

under-budget.def: The gold standard of corporate delivery: achieving all milestones prior to deadline while expending less capital than authorized.
under-budget.quote: Louie (26:36): "My primary mandate was to deliver the project on time and under budget, which is most of my work."
under-budget.l1: 納期厳守かつ予算内で (超過なしのプロジェクト遂行)

who-dares-wins.def: The British military and business maxim that courage, bold calculated risks, and stubborn grit will conquer seemingly impossible obstacles.
who-dares-wins.quote: Louie (15:08): "What I learned from this process is that 'who dares wins'. Where there's a will, there's a way."
who-dares-wins.l1: 勇気ある者が勝つ / 挑む者に勝利は微笑む

where-theres-a-will.word: where there's a will, there's a way
where-theres-a-will.def: Proverb affirming that intense determination and resolve can overcome any procedural or bureaucratic barrier.
where-theres-a-will.quote: Louie (15:08): "Where there's a will, there's a way. We just have to sometimes suck it up and put the effort and work in."
where-theres-a-will.l1: 意志あるところに道は開ける

suck-it-up.def: To stoically endure an exhausting physical effort or stressful hardship without quitting or making excuses.
suck-it-up.quote: Louie (15:08): "We just have to sometimes suck it up and put the effort and the work in... Anything is possible, even under the most extreme circumstances."
suck-it-up.l1: 文句を言わず耐え抜く / 覚悟を決めてやり抜く

shot-yourself-in-the-foot.def: To inadvertently destroy one's own advantage or mislead one's own investigation through an unfortunate mistake.
shot-yourself-in-the-foot.quote: Louie (07:12): "I think you shot yourself in the foot about asking about Vietnam because Vietnam has a strange relationship with this bird."
shot-yourself-in-the-foot.l1: 自分で自分の首を絞める / 墓穴を掘る / 足を引っ張る

bog-down.def: To become heavily delayed, overwhelmed, or bogged down by excessive trivia and non-essential considerations.
bog-down.quote: Louie (06:05): "I think you got too bogged down in vegetables and everything like that."
bog-down.l1: 些末な点に行き詰まる / 泥沼にはまる

misalignment.def: A divergence in goals, expectations, or priorities between departments, leaders, or operational reports.
misalignment.quote: Louie (36:30): "Maybe there's a misalignment in your reporting skills or something..."
misalignment.l1: 認識の不一致 / 方向性のズレ

out-of-the-loop.def: Excluded from vital updates, critical developments, or insider intelligence within an organization.
out-of-the-loop.quote: Louie (34:56): "So, I see you're out of the loop, you have the information, but it's not coming."
out-of-the-loop.l1: 情報共有から外れて / 蚊帳の外で

put-in-their-shoes.def: To evaluate an issue or strategic presentation from the specific vantage point, pressures, and priorities of another executive.
put-in-their-shoes.quote: YH (37:17): "Well, first of all, what I learned is I always need to put myself in their shoes, which is seeing the situation from his angle."
put-in-their-shoes.l1: 相手の立場に身を置く / 相手の目線で物事を捉える

operational.def: Practical expertise in running daily business logistics, supply chain routines, workflow optimization, and execution.
operational.quote: Louie (40:43): "However, I need to improve my operational skills. / YH: Operations and management skills."
operational.l1: 業務推進力 / 運用管理の実務スキル

aspirations.def: High-level ambitions, long-range career milestones, and visionary corporate targets.
aspirations.quote: Louie (40:43): "Nice. So your aspirations... are that I would like to have my own business."
aspirations.l1: 大志 / キャリア上の抱負 / 長期的な目標

attribute.def: A distinctive executive trait, characteristic behavior, or leadership philosophy exhibited by a manager.
attribute.quote: Louie (43:30): "And what is one management attribute that you would like to develop?"
attribute.l1: マネジメント資質 / 指導力の特徴

overhaul.def: Completely dismantling, redesigning, and modernizing a system or process from top to bottom.
overhaul.quote: Louie (26:36): "I'm tired because I've been spending the last few days overhauling the notes even more... Now, a new system completely."
overhaul.l1: 全面刷新する / 抜本的に見直して作り直す

meritocracy.def: A system where status and promotion are awarded purely on demonstrable competence and quantifiable results.
meritocracy.quote: Louie (45:40): "I think I would like to develop an environment where we do not only rely on merit. Maybe there is a place for everyone in the team."
meritocracy.l1: 実力・成果主義 (純粋な実績のみを評価基準とすること)

combative.def: Aggressively contentious, combative, or fiercely competitive in tone or team culture.
combative.quote: Louie (45:40): "Maybe there is a place for everyone in the team and it's not so combative in competing, I think."
combative.l1: 好戦的な / 対立的で刺々しい

tackle.def: To aggressively initiate action and confront a complex operational obstacle.
tackle.quote: Louie (26:36): "Okay, so in action, we can use, obviously, first... or to tackle the problem, to tackle this task, I did blah."
tackle.l1: 課題に果敢に取り組む / 正面から対処する

direct-result.word: as a direct result of my actions
direct-result.def: Explicitly establishing executive causality between your personal actions and business performance.
direct-result.quote: Louie (26:36): "Next result, the nice one: as a direct result of my actions. Okay, nice and easy."
direct-result.l1: 私の施策の直接的な成果として

looking-back.def: Examining past decisions with critical hindsight and seasoned perspective.
looking-back.quote: Louie (26:36): "Looking back, I would never have owned a bar. Or if I were to do this again..."
looking-back.l1: 今にして思えば / 当時を振り返ってみると

sales-driving.def: The pivotal product offerings, customer segments, or marketing channels that generate the overwhelming majority of revenue.
sales-driving.quote: YH (19:11): "And that we can more focus on the sales driving factors. So yeah, this is my responsibility that time."
sales-driving.l1: 売上を牽引する中核要因 / トップライン成長のレバー

best-selling.def: Merchandise enjoying the highest sales volume, conversion rate, and transaction frequency in a catalog.
best-selling.quote: YH (12:37): "So we always analyze the data and we keep picking up on the best-selling items or best-selling brands."
best-selling.l1: 売れ筋商品 / 最多販売アイテム

product-lines.def: A family of related commercial products marketed by a retail business to satisfy specific consumer segments.
product-lines.quote: Louie (22:02): "So we can use the word, say, instead of add additional: we can have additional product lines or items..."
product-lines.l1: 製品ライン / 商品カテゴリー群

planning-permission.def: Formal statutory approval required from local government authorities for physical property development and zoning.
planning-permission.quote: Louie (15:08): "A situation that I was involved in was that I needed to get some planning permission approved..."
planning-permission.l1: 都市計画・建築開発許可

fermented.def: Foods transformed through controlled microbial fermentation, such as natto, miso, or kimchi.
fermented.quote: Louie (05:13): "For example, I think in Japan you can eat rice and egg mixed together or little fermented things..."
fermented.l1: 発酵食品 (納豆や味噌など)

remortgaging.def: Refinancing an existing property loan to obtain emergency capital or stave off corporate insolvency.
remortgaging.quote: Louie (26:36): "Their cost was 2 million. Insane. They were remortgaging, and it is a horrible thing to see."
remortgaging.l1: 再担保設定 / 住宅ローンの借り換え (資金繰りの窮策)

organic.def: Derived from living matter without synthetic chemicals; natural biological organism.
organic.quote: Louie (08:15): "Okay... Is it organic? / YH: Yes."
organic.l1: 有機の / 動植物由来の

e-commerce.def: Digital commercial transactions conducted across networked platforms and electronic retail storefronts.
e-commerce.quote: YH (12:37): "For example, e-commerce, when I was working in the e-commerce, you have a lot of customer data and item data..."
e-commerce.l1: 電子商取引 / Eコマース事業

oversee.def: To hold operational command, fiduciary responsibility, and general governance over a large workforce.
oversee.quote: Louie (42:40): "Wow. So you oversaw 100 employees. / YH: Right, yeah."
oversee.l1: 100名の組織を統括・指揮した

voice.def: To audibly register grievances, training inadequacies, or operational risks before small cracks become crises.
voice.quote: Louie (24:48): "My problem as an employee was I would not voice problems with my training... So I got in big trouble for this."
voice.l1: 問題点や懸念を進んで口に出す / 声を上げる

unusual.def: Remarkable, non-standard, or distinct from habitual cultural expectations.
unusual.quote: Louie (03:51): "It's not unusual, but maybe it sounds unusual, but it's not unusual at all."
unusual.l1: 普通ではない / 珍しい / 異例の

concept.def: A generalized cultural construct or mental model governing social habits.
concept.quote: Louie (05:13): "In Vietnam, they don't have the concept of breakfast. They will just eat dinner again, which is... very weird to have a full meal."
concept.l1: 朝食という概念 / 観念
